metadata.description: Knowbility — plugins for accessible software delivery. Each one is small, focused, and standalone; none depends on another.

plugins.name: know-product-spec
plugins.description: v0.2.0 — Interviews you and writes a product spec an engineer can build from. Starts by testing whether the thing is worth building at all, and will tell you when it isn't. Then asks how it behaves, drafts the document, and grades its own draft by breaking it into workstreams and tasks, reporting every decision it had to invent so you can close the gap before someone else guesses. The contract it asks for includes how the thing is operated and what it announces — the keyboard path, where focus goes on each state change, the name of every control whose meaning is not carried by visible text, which field a validation error names and how to recover — because those are behavior two builders will otherwise guess differently, and the grader treats an unstated one as blocking. Once the work is filed it keeps going: grooming works a list of tickets with you, resolving, sharpening, or routing each one to whoever owns the call, and a UI review opens every surface a story needs in a browser, exercises it, and returns a readiness verdict with every finding traced to a contract (it needs browser tools in the session). Built for software product teams, tracker-agnostic, with your local vocabulary and style in an optional profile. Standalone.

plugins.name: know-qa-agent
plugins.description: v0.2.0 — Point it at any web app and it tests like a skeptical engineer, then reports what broke and why, with the evidence. A deterministic engine tracks the full test matrix so requested coverage can't silently disappear. Accessibility runs in two tiers: baseline checks ride along in every test — keyboard reachability, visible focus, alt text, form labels, obvious contrast problems — and a deeper tier you turn on per test adds the bundled axe-core ruleset and WCAG AA contrast ratios computed from resolved colors, each finding carrying the success criteria it maps to. Every accessibility run also reports its own coverage across all 55 live Level A/AA criteria, in four grades it never merges — a rule failed, a rule could not decide, a rule ran and found nothing, and no rule reaches it at all — so "no violations" cannot be read as "no problems" and the untested criteria come out as a named work list. Anything the tools cannot resolve is reported as needs-review rather than guessed, and none of it is a conformance evaluation or a substitute for testing by a person. Findings come back triaged, deduplicated, and ready to file, and a team can split the app into owned areas with roll-ups posted to Slack. Standalone.

plugins.name: know-security
plugins.description: v0.1.0 — Read the code the way someone trying to get at the data would read it. An adversarial security and privacy reviewer that runs alongside development, hunting the endpoint nobody remembered, the helper everyone uses except here, the log line that seemed harmless, and the personal data no deletion path reaches. Reports findings — severity, the attack path as read, the input that exercises it, the blast radius, the fix — across authorization, PII data flow, injection, authentication, secrets, XSS, SSRF, crypto, config, audit trails and dependencies. Confidence is welded to evidence type so it cannot claim exploitability without naming an input, and seven known-benign classes plus a read-before-classify rule keep it from crying wolf. Scripts locate candidates and say what they could not read; the agent judges. Never probes the system under review and never holds its credentials; the only network access is the dependency check running your project's own package auditor against your package registry, the same thing `npm audit` does. Standalone.

plugins.name: know-photo-generator
plugins.description: v0.2.0 — Get a professional-grade photo from a plain-language description, without knowing what a key light or an 85mm prime is. A guided workflow turns your scene into a physics-aware Nano Banana Pro prompt — camera body, lens, lighting setup, and color grade chosen from a curated reference library — then generates the image directly via the Gemini API at the right aspect ratio for print, social, or hero-banner use. Every run ends with a drafted text alternative: it asks what job the image does where it lands — decorative, informative, or functional — and writes the alt-text draft beside the file for the person placing it to approve. /know-photo:setup handles the API key (pasted into a local keys.env, never the chat) and an optional default house style; batch and variations modes cover shot lists and multiple takes. Standalone; runs on its own.

plugins.name: know-blueprint
plugins.description: v0.2.0 — Turn how you actually work into a structured process model. A guided interview extracts what people forget to write down — triggers, data movement, decision criteria, exceptions, approval authority — then rates every step Automate, Monitor, or Human so you know where automation is safe and where a human must stay in the loop. The ratings are a reviewed draft, not a safety certification, until a stakeholder signs off, which validate is how you run — it walks the ratings one at a time with the person who owns the risk, pressure-tests the exception paths, and records what the pass did not cover, so a partial review never reads as a complete one, and any step that turns on accessibility judgment defaults to Human. Discover sweeps your recurring work into a process inventory when you can't yet name your processes; capture models a process you already run; design models a new one you don't yet, proposing an intended flow grounded in your real constraints and nearest analog, never invented. Five entry points: discover, capture, design, validate, and a guide that routes you. Standalone; runs on its own.

plugins.name: know-researcher
plugins.description: v1.18.1 — Get research you can stand behind, not a confident summary that might be invented. Describe your research challenge and work through a phased plan grounded in it: collecting sources, finding patterns, mapping gaps, synthesizing findings, and auditing every claim back to its source note — and every note to a declared source. Decisions the project records — corrections, resolutions, accepted gaps, your own directives — are durable, and no later draft can quietly walk one back. Completion is gated by your stated success criteria and an independent adversarial review of the whole corpus. Confidence tiers rate how well the evidence supports a claim, nothing more: a sourced finding about an accessibility requirement is a reading of the standard, not a conformance determination about any product. A research partner, not a summarizer. Standalone; runs on its own.
